A1.justification: Both PDFs describe R-WoM, with matching authors, core framework, probing tasks and benchmarks. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original probing results, OSWorld/WebArena evaluations, grounding and horizon experiments, and retrieval/cost analyses in Tables 1–2 and Appendix A.4.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds tutorial-scarce experiments, efficiency measurements, failure analyses and ablations in Section 5.5 and Appendices A.4–A.6.

M1.justification: v2 adds adaptive action branching and semantic deduplication that can bypass world-model rollouts, plus a two-stage trajectory-to-tutorial synthesis/consolidation procedure. The reported OSWorld action interface also changes from higher-level operations such as opening applications and setting spreadsheet cells to explicit clicks and keys. Retrieval grounding, LongCoT simulation and listwise ranking already existed in v1.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates tutorial-covered subsets and leaves tutorial-scarce environments to future work. v2 evaluates OSWorld tasks lacking existing tutorials, supported by approximately 1.3k tutorials synthesized from 2k AgentNet trajectories (Section 5.5, Table 3). This substantially extends the tested conditions while retaining the original benchmark families.

E2.justification: v1's main world-model comparator is WoM, explicitly a LongCoT adaptation of WebDreamer; v2 instead specifies iterative WebDreamer in Section 5.1 and Table 2. v1's cost table lists these as separate methods, establishing a substantive change in the reported comparator. Identical retained comparator scores and residual WoM labels leave implementation consistency and rerunning unresolved.

E3.justification: v2 introduces retrieval-conditioned planning evaluation, Claude-4/4.5 backbones, alternative LLM judges, adaptive/full-rollout controls, absolute reward scoring and candidate counts of 2, 3 and 5. Oracle annotation changes from one or two chunks to one, and the reported OSWorld action space changes. Section 5.1 now states 87 OSWorld tasks, but Appendix A.2 retains 85, so an actual subset-size revision is not established.

E4.justification: Appendices A.4–A.6 add adaptive efficiency analysis, retrieval-failure examples and counts, failure categorization, cross-judge checks, and reward-design/candidate-size ablations. The earlier domain-level success analysis and full call-count/runtime comparison are removed or replaced. Existing grounding, horizon and retrieval-strategy analyses are retained; the retrieval plot is moved into the main text.

E5.justification: Table 2 continues to report three runs with the same uncertainty notation and uncertainty values. No new seed information, repeated-run policy, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure is introduced. Additional ablations report point estimates, as earlier ablations did.

E6.justification: All six Table 2 R-WoM means are revised downward; for example, Qwen's OSWorld/WebArena values change from 38.05/28.92 to 37.48/28.49, while its leading rank remains. Table 1 adds planning-with-retrieval results, and new tables report tutorial-scarce, efficiency, failure and ablation outcomes. v1's domain and detailed runtime results disappear. Changed reported methods/settings prevent treating the revised means as controlled performance regressions.

T1.justification: The background, probing definitions and core rollout/reward equations remain substantively unchanged. Retrieval-equation notation is edited, but no new formal assumptions, theoretical properties, derivations or proofs are supplied.

C1.justification: The central claims about tutorial grounding and longer-horizon world modeling remain. v2 narrows the abstract's empirical claim to relative improvements on benchmark subsets and revises the maximum claimed gains from 25.3%/18.1% to 23.4%/16.3% for OSWorld/WebArena.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of generation-dominated cost, adaptive efficiency, filtering and fallback under irrelevant retrieval, and difficulties with ambiguous goals and content modification. It removes v1's domain-specific interpretation and the conclusion's explicit caveats about tutorial availability, outdated documentation and remaining cost. Applicability and failure mechanisms receive substantially different treatment.

D1.justification: Appendices A.2–A.3 provide new synthesis, consolidation, adaptive-branching and deduplication prompts, skill-format requirements, trajectory provenance and a test-task nonoverlap statement. Action/output specifications are revised. Cost documentation changes from the earlier cross-benchmark call-count/runtime table to retrieval latency, trigger reductions and token accounting.

R1.justification: v2 adds WorldGPT, WALL-E, LiteCUA, OpenCUA/AgentNet and procedural-memory/skill-induction references. The introduction distinguishes computer-use grounding from prior video and simulated-environment grounding, while synthesis is linked to procedural memory. The established positioning of inference-time tutorial grounding relative to offline trajectory generation remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative and much background/probing prose are retained. v2 revises method, setup and retrieval explanations, adds RQ4 and an ethics/reproducibility section, and reorganizes the empirical appendix around cost, failures and ablations. The LLM-use disclosure moves from A.5 to A.7, and publication headers change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to show synthetic tutorials and adaptive rollout paths; Table 1 gains a retrieval column, and numerous new tables replace the former domain/runtime displays. The retrieval plot moves from v1 Figure 8 to v2 Figure 3 and is restyled. Existing grounding, horizon and probing illustrations are retained and renumbered; prompt boxes and table formatting also change.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens practical and empirical support by testing tutorial-scarce operation and adaptive cost reduction, both explicit future-work concerns in v1. Reward-design, candidate-size and judge ablations, failure analyses and implementation prompts also address previously untested explanations and reproducibility needs. These gains outweigh the loss of domain/runtime breakdowns. However, conflicting subset counts and insufficiently reconciled comparator and main-versus-appendix results remain material reporting weaknesses.
